title: Finland – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Perustietotekniikkapalveluiden hankinta - Osallistumispyyntö
description: Jyväskylän kaupunki (jäljempänä "Hankintayksikkö" tai "Tilaaja") järjestää hankintalain (1397/2016) mukaisen tarjouskilpailun perustietotekniikkapalveluiden hankinnassa. Hankintayksikkö pyytää ehdokkaita lähettämään osallistumishakemuksen kilpailulliseen neuvottelumenettelyyn tämän osallistumispyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Hankinnan kohteena ovat seuraavat perustietotekniikkapalveluiden palvelukokonaisuudet: 1. Käyttäjätukipalvelut, jonka sisältämät palvelut ovat tarpeen tietoteknistä ympäristöä käyttävien henkilöiden IT-ongelmien ratkaisemiseksi, käytön neuvonnaksi ja työntekemisen tukemiseksi; 2. Päätelaitteiden elinkaaripalvelut, joka sisältää kattavan joukon palveluita varmistamaan työasemien ja mobiililaitteiden ja niiden lisälaitteiden tehokkaan, turvallisen ja kustannustehokkaan käytön niiden koko elinkaaren ajan. Kokonaisuus sisältää myös työasemalaitteiden hankinnan; 3. Palvelinten käyttöpalvelut, jonka sisältämät palvelut ovat keskeisiä palvelininfrastruktuurin ja sitä tukevan tietoliikenneinfrastruktuurin osalta ja joiden avulla varmistetaan palvelinten tehokas ja luotettava toiminta sekä hallinta; 4. Pilvipalvelut, jonka sisältämät palvelut tarjoavat julkisten pilvipalveluiden keskitetyn hallinnan ja valvonnan pilvipohjaisille resursseille ja palveluille; 5. Tietoturvapalvelut, joka sisältää kattavan joukon palveluita, joiden tavoitteena on suojata tietoteknistä ympäristöä kaikenlaisilta uhilta ja riskeiltä, sisältäen mm. ennaltaehkäisevät toimenpiteet, aktiivisen seurannan, tunkeutumisen havaitsemisen ja reagoinnin sekä jatkuvan tietoturvatason parantamisen; 6. Identiteetin- ja pääsynhallinta, joka sisältää palveluita, jotka keskittyvät henkilöstön, kumppaneiden, tietojärjestelmien identiteettien, pääsynvalvonnan ja oikeuksien hallintaan sekä niitä tukevien tietojärjestelmien ja julkisten pilvipalveluiden hallintaan; 7. Asiantuntijapalvelut, sisältävät erikoistuneeseen ammatilliseen asiantuntijatyöhön ja konsultointiin liittyvät palvelut, jotka tukevat IT-infrastruktuuria, tietojärjestelmiä, tietoturvan ja toiminnan suunnittelua, optimointia, kehittämistä, laajentamista sekä uudistamista; sekä 8. Palvelunhallinta, joka sisältää hankittavan palvelukokonaisuuden hallintaan ja kehittämiseen liittyvät palvelut sekä IT-prosesseihin liittyvät palvelut. Perustietotekniikkapalveluiden kokonaisuuksien sisältö on alustava ja tarkentuu neuvotteluissa. Hankintaa koskevat asiakirjat ja niiden sisältö täydentyvät hankintamenettelyn aikana ja lopullinen hankinnan kohde ja vaatimukset esitetään lopullisessa tarjouspyynnössä. title: Finland – Dismantling works – Kielotie 28:n toimisto- ja liikerakennuksen purku-urakka
description: Kiinteistö Oy Lehdokkitien Virastotalo pyytää tarjoustanne Kielotie 28:n toimisto- ja liikerakennuksen purku-urakasta kiinteähintaisena kokonaisurakkana tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liiteasiakirjojen mukaisesti. Hankinta toteutetaan avoimella menettelyllä. Purku-urakan kohde on vuonna 1983 valmistunut toimisto- ja liikerakennus, jonka bruttopinta-ala on 6 967 m2. Rakennuksessa on kaksi osaa. Osassa A on neljä kerrosta, kellarikerros sekä osittainen ullakkokerros. Rakennus on perustettu paalujen varaan. Alapohja ja maanvastaiset seinät ovat betonirakenteiset. Rakennuksen runko on paikalla valettu ja se koostuu kantavista ulkoseinistä ja pilaripalkkirungosta. A-osan kellarikerroksessa on sosiaalitiloja, teknisiä tiloja, varastoja ja rakennuksen väestönsuojatilat. B-osa on kolmikerroksinen ja kauttaaltaan nostettu betonipilarien varaan. B-osassa on toimistotiloja kerroksissa 2–4. Väliseinät ovat molemmissa rakennusosissa pääosin muurattuja ja toimistotilojen välillä kevytrakenteisia siirtoseiniä. Rakennuksen vesikattona on bitumikermikatto, sisäpuolisella vedenpoistolla. Rakennuksessa ei ole tehty kattavaa peruskorjausta ja se on pinnoiltaan pääosin alkuperäisessä kunnossa. Kielotie 28:n kortteli on Vantaan kaupunkiympäristön toimialan toimintojen pääasiallisessa käytössä aiemmin ollut toimisto- ja liikerakennus, joka on nyttemmin tyhjentynyt ja poistettu käytöstä. Kaupunkikonsernissa on tehty päätökset kohteen purkamisesta. Kohteen omistaa Kiinteistö Oy Lehdokkitien Virastotalo, jonka osakekannan omistavat yhdessä Vantaan kaupunki ja kaupunkikonserniin kuuluva Vivamus Kiinteistöt Oy. Osakkaat ovat sopineet, että Vivamus Kiinteistöt Oy ohjaa ja koordinoi purku-ukakkaa. Vivamus Kiinteistöt Oy on tehnyt mm. purku-urakassa tarvittavat suunnittelu- ja asiantuntijapalvelusopimukset lukuunsa. Kiinteistö Oy Lehdokkitien Virastotalo pyytää tällä tarjouspyynnöllä tarjouksia kohteen purku-urakasta, jonka tarkempi laajuus ilmenee tarjouspyynnön liitteenä olevista asiakirjoista. TÄRKEÄ HUOMIOITAVA - URAKKAPAIKAN ESITTELY: Tilaaja edellyttää, että urakoitsija tutustuu urakkapaikkaan ennen tarjouksen antamista. Urakkapaikan esittelytilaisuudet pidetään paikan päällä 18.11.2026 klo 12.00 ja 19.11.2026 klo 12.00.

title: Service Contract for Carl Zeiss LSM 900 Confocal Microscope System
description: 75N98027Q00067 Service Contract for Carl Zeiss LSM 900 Confocal Microscope System The National Institutes of Health (NIH), National Cancer Institute (NCI), intends to award a contract to Carl Zeiss on a sole-source basis pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements, for the acquisition of LSM 900 / Axio Observer 7, the Government intends to solicit and award a Purchase Order on a sole-source basis because the Government's minimum technical requirements will be satisfied by Carl Zeiss. The National Institutes of Health (NIH) / National Cancer Institute (NCI) utilizes high-resolution optical microscopy platforms to support advanced biomedical research and critical imaging requirements. The Laboratory currently operates a Carl Zeiss LSM 900 confocal laser scanning microscope system mounted on an Axio Observer 7 motorized inverted microscope stand, equipped with an Airyscan detector module and GaAsP detectors (Serial Number: 2901001023). To prevent instrument downtime, maintain optical alignment and detector calibration, ensure compliance with evolving IT security and operating system environments, and protect scientific data integrity, ongoing manufacturer-certified preventative maintenance, unscheduled corrective repairs, and software support are required. Carl Zeiss Microscopy, LLC is the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) capable of supplying certified factory-trained service engineers and proprietary parts to service this specialized research equipment. The primary objective of this requirement is to acquire a comprehensive 12-month Protect Premium Service Agreement and Software Maintenance Agreement (SMA) for the Government-owned ZEISS LSM 900 / Axio Observer 7 confocal microscope system. Specifically, the agreement will provide: Preventative Maintenance: One (1) annual comprehensive preventative maintenance (PM) inspection visit. Remedial Repairs: Unlimited on-site remedial corrective repair service visits, inclusive of all labor, travel, and covered replacement parts. Software Maintenance: Software Maintenance Agreement (SMA) coverage for the ZEN software suite (ZEN w/ Advanced Acquisition and ZEN Band C), including regular version updates/upgrades, bug fixes, and patch releases. Technical Support: Ongoing remote technical support and prioritized call handling to maximize instrument uptime for NCI research operations. Carl Zeiss is the original manufacturer and sole supplier of the LSM 900 / Axio Observer 7. This piece of equipment utilizes Droplet Digital PCR for the absolute quantification of nucleic acids. This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required supplies and meet all specified technical and operational requirements. The Government will consider all timely capability statements received and determine whether the acquisition should proceed as a sole-source procurement or be competed. The Government anticipates making an award approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source is capable of meeting the requirement. Capability statements shall be submitted electronically to davisroshonna@mail.nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on November 20, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98027Q00067 in the subject line of the response.

description: Description: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police in Iqaluit, Nunavut Territories, has a requirement for Generator Inspection & Maintenance Services at the RCMP Cambridge Bay, Clyde River, Gjoa Haven, Kinngait, Qikitarjuaq, Taloyoak Detachments, Iqaluit Headquarters Building and Iqaluit Hangar. This procurement is subject to the Nunavut Land Claims Agreement and the Directive on Government Contracts, Including Real Property Leases, in the Nunavut Settlement Area. Bidders are requested to maximize Inuit employment, subcontracting and on-the-job training opportunities, and involve Inuit businesses, in carrying out the work under this project. The Nunavut Agreement contains a provision requiring the inclusion of socio-economic bid criteria in the solicitation document, when practicable and consistent with sound procurement management principles. These socio-economic bid criteria are referred to as Nunavut Benefits Criteria (NBC) and Inuit Benefits Criteria (IBC), and bidders propose Inuit benefits in their bid submission via an Inuit Benefits Plan (IBP). This solicitation is limited for bidding among firms registered on the Inuit Firm Registry (IFR). Bids submitted by businesses not on the IFR will render the bid non-responsive and no further consideration will be accorded to the bid. Delivery Date: The contract period will be for 36-months from the date of contract, with the option to extend for 2 additional 1 year periods. Security: This requirement contains a security requirement. Basis of selection: A bid must comply with all the requirements of the bid solicitation and meet all mandatory requirements. Bids not meeting the requirements will be declared non-responsive. The selection will be based on the highest responsive combined rating of total Inuit Benefits Plan (IBP) merit, and price. The ratio will be 30% for the total IBP merit, and 70% for price. Tenders must be submitted to the RCMP Bid Receiving Unit at: NWR_Procurement_Bids@rcmp-grc.gc.ca Refer to the attached tender documents to obtain further information. Canada retains the right to negotiate with any supplier on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. As a result, the integrity provisions are being applied in RCMP contracting activities as outlined in this solicitation. Canada will make available Notices of Proposed Procurement (NPP), bid solicitations and related documents for download through the Government Electronic Tendering Service (GETS) at https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities . Canada is not responsible and will not assume any liabilities whatsoever for the information found on websites of third parties. In the event an NPP, bid solicitation or related documentation would be amended, Canada will not be sending notifications. Canada will post all amendments, including significant enquiries received and their replies, using GETS. It is the sole responsibility of the Bidder to regularly consult GETS for the most up-to-date information. Canada will not be liable for any oversight on the Bidder's part nor for notification services offered by a third party. Having a business profile in the IBD will increase your company’s visibility and may provide additional business. A profile in the IBD can also allow you to compete for federal government contracts that are set-aside for Indigenous businesses through the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Businesses. title: Klimawandelgerechte Transformation des DDR-Typenhauses Körnerstraße 9-10 in 99099 Erfurt. Los 06_Spezialtiefbau / Großbohrpfähle
description: Allgemeine Angaben zur Baustelle: Die 11-geschossige Wohnscheibe Körnerstraße 9-10 ist Bestandteil des Modellvorhabens zur Weiterentwicklung der Städebauförderung Erfurt Südost. Die Wohnscheibe liegt in exponierter Lage am Kammweg und ist dadurch im Stadtbild weithin sichtbar. Die Großwohnsiedlung Herrenberg ist in den 1970er Jahren entstanden, das Objekt Körnerstraße wurde Anfang der 1980er Jahre errichtet. Durch die Herstellung einer Gebäudefuge zwischen der Körnerstraße 9 und 10 wird die massive Wirkung des Gebäudes aufgelöst. Der Haupteingang des Gebäudes erfolgt über einen dreigeschossigen Neubau innerhalb der Gebäudefuge. Die Erschließung der sanierten Wohnungen erfolgt über vorgesetzte Laubengänge. Die Körnerstraße 10 erhält einen Anbau für Tagespflegeeinrichtungen und Seniorenresidenz. Der Auftrag umfasst die prüffähige Werkstatt- und Montageplanung auf Grundlage der bauseitigen Tragwerksplanung sowie die Herstellung bewehrter Ortbeton-Großbohrpfähle im verrohrten Kelly-Verfahren. Eingeschlossen sind Baustelleneinrichtung, Vermessung, erforderliche Erdarbeiten zur Herstellung und Wiederherrichtung der Arbeitsflächen und Baustraßen sowie Abtransport und fachgerechte Entsorgung des Bohrguts. Hinzu kommen die Kampfmitteluntersuchung der Bohrpfahlstandorte einschließlich Freigabedokumentation sowie die Lieferung und Integration von Geothermie-Spiralkollektoren in die Pfähle, einschließlich Druckprüfung und dokumentierter Übergabe an das Folgegewerk. Zum Leistungsumfang gehören ferner Beweissicherung, Betonüberwachung, Pfahlintegritätsprüfungen sowie die vollständigen Dokumentations-, Prüf-, Entsorgungs- und Revisionsnachweise. Die Ausführung erfolgt unter beengten Platzverhältnissen und in Abstimmung mit den parallel tätigen Gewerken sowie dem vorgegebenen Bauablauf. Einzelheiten zu Art und Umfang der Leistungen sowie den technischen Anforderungen ergeben sich aus dem Leistungsverzeichnis „24-241 L06 Spezialtiefbau / Großbohrpfähle“ einschließlich der zugehörigen Anlagen.

description: Notice Type: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Title: Mobile Phone Services � U.S. Embassy Lusaka, Zambia Solicitation Number: 19ZA6026Q0008 NAICS Code: 517112 Set-Aside: None (Unrestricted) Place of Performance: Lusaka, Zambia Response Date: 20 November 2026, 5:00 p.m. CAT Point of Contact: Lusaka-procurement@state.gov | +260 211 357000 Description: The U.S. Embassy in Lusaka, Zambia, requests quotations for mobile phone services for official Embassy use. The contractor will provide voice, data, SMS, voicemail, international calling, international roaming, itemized billing, and 24/7 customer support for about 550 subscriptions on Government-furnished devices. The contractor must provide at least 90% network coverage within Zambia, with 5G/LTE or newer technology widely available in Lusaka, the surrounding areas, and the provincial capitals. The Embassy will award a single indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract with a one-year base period (2 January 2027 � 1 January 2028) and four one-year option periods. The Embassy will award to the responsible offeror whose quotation offers the best value, using comparative evaluation under FAR 13.106-2(b)(3). Each quotation must include a completed Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management (C-SCRM) Questionnaire or an acceptable third-party assessment, such as ISO 27001 or SOC II. The Embassy will rate it go/no-go. Offerors must be registered in SAM.gov when they submit their quotations. Pre-Quotation Conference: 3 November 2026, 10:00 a.m. (local time), U.S. Embassy Lusaka. Contact Lusaka-procurement@state.gov by 28 October 2026 to attend. Submission: Email quotations to Lusaka-procurement@state.gov in English, in MS Word, Excel, or PDF format. Each email must be under 30 MB. The Embassy will not accept late or incomplete quotations. See the attached RFQ for full requirements, clauses, and evaluation criteria.

title: 4610--FY27 Portable Reverse Osmosis (RO) Water Purification System
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office 8, hereby provides notice of its intent to award a sole-source, firm fixed, contract to Evoqua Water Technologies LLC, 111 47TH ST, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, 15201-2901, United States. The contract is expected to be awarded IAW FAR 13.106-1(1), soliciting from a single source, the VA has determined this BRAND NAME ONLY requirement is limited to only one responsible source that can provide the supplies or services at the level of quality required because the supplies or services are unique or highly specialized. The contract will be a firm fixed price contract with the NAICS Code of 221310 with a small business size standard of $41 Million. A Sole Source Justification has been prepared. title: USACE SPK DBB Construction - Sacramento River East Levee Contract 5 (SREL C5), Sacramento, California
description: ** Update 11/12/2026 - Prject Title, Project description, and anticipated project magnitude have been updated.** Solicitation Number: W9123827X1CQR Sacramento River East Levee Contract 5 (SREL 5), Sacramento, CA The United States Army Corps of Engineers {USACE) Sacramento District (SPK) anticipates a potential levee repair and remediation requirement located within the City of Sacramento, California, along segments of the Sacramento River East Levee (SREL) to the south of downtown Sacramento. The combined length of the levee segments to be remediated under this contract is approximately 0.4 miles. The Contractor must furnish all labor, material, equipment, quality control and supervision required to complete the work. The work includes, but is not limited to: providing and maintaining all temporary facilities; implementing stormwater pollution prevention plan requirements; complying with all applicable permit requirements and environmental mitigation measures; developing staging areas designated for Contractor's use to the extent needed; coordinating with Agencies and stakeholders as necessary; construction of seepage and stability berms and buried curb walls in various locations; researching, potholing, removing and replacing existing utilities; protecting existing utilities, reusing excavated soils that meet specification criteria for reuse as levee fill; importing soil for levee fill as necessary; managing and disposing of excess excavated soils; removing all temporary facilities; and restoring and vegetating all disturbed areas. All contractor and subcontractor personnel performing work under this contract must be citizens of the United States. U.S. citizenship is a prerequisite for obtaining the required Department of War (DoW) personnel security clearances. The contractor shall be responsible for ensuring all personnel comply with this requirement and all applicable federal security regulations. The solicitation is anticipated to proceed as a total small business set-aside and is estimated to be issued late- November 2026 with bids due tentatively in late-December 2026. The IFB will be issued on the Government Point of Entry known as SAM.gov and will establish a firm bid due date/time. The magnitude of construction for the anticipated project is between $6,000,000 and $9,000,000. This solicitation is anticipated to be issued using the North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code 237990 (Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction). The small business size standard is $45,000,000. Product Service Code is Y1LC (Construction of Tunnels and Subsurface Structures). If applicable, the site visit date, time and location will be identified in the solicitation. BE ADVISED THAT THIS PROJECT MAY BE DELAYED, CANCELLED OR REVISED AT ANY TIME DURING THE PRE-SOLICITATION, SOLICITATION, SELECTION, EVALUATION, NEGOTIATION AND/OR FINAL AWARD PROCESS. The only INTERESTED VENDORS LISTS (plan-holder's/bidder's list) are available via SAM.gov. Contractors are responsible for self-identifying as interested vendors and viewing other interested vendors. Contractors should check SAM.gov frequently for any changes to the interested vendors list and notice. PLEASE DO NOT request a copy of the solicitation, or draft plans and specifications, as they are not currently available. Any available technical data required to respond to the solicitation will be furnished as part of the solicitation. Following solicitation release, all responsible sources may submit a bid that shall be considered by the agency. This project and/or the anticipated solicitation may be changed, delayed, or canceled at any time. All prospective Offerors and their Subcontractors must be registered in SAM and the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) websites to download solicitation information. Solicitation documents, plans, and specifications will only be available to be downloaded from PIEE, which may be accessed at https://piee.eb.mil/. Registration should be completed one (1) week prior to the anticipated solicitation release date. USACE-SPK will not notify Offerors of any changes to the solicitation; Offerors must monitor PIEE and SAM for the solicitation to be posted, and for any posted changes or amendments.

title: USACE SPK DBB Construction - Sacramento River East Levee Contract 5 (SREL C5), Sacramento, California
description: Solicitation Number: W9123827X1CQR Sacramento River Erosion (SRE) Pioneer Bridge Levee Improvements, Sacramento, CA The Government anticipates issuing a Design-Bid-Build (DB) Invitation for Bid (IFB) with the intent of awarding a Firm-Fixed Price construction contract for Sacramento River Erosion (SRE) Pioneer Bridge Levee Improvements. Project Description: Project is design-bid-build construction services to construct levee improvements at Sacramento River Erosion (SRE) Site 1, located under the I-80 Pioneer Bridge in Sacramento, California (CA). The project is anticipated to reduce the risk of levee failure from an erosion related levee breach for approximately 0.4 miles along the Sacramento River. The Contractor must furnish all labor, material, equipment, quality control and supervision required to complete the work. The work includes, but is not limited to: providing and maintaining all temporary facilities; implementing stormwater pollution prevention plan requirements; complying with all applicable permit requirements and environmental mitigation measures; developing staging areas designated for Contractor's use to the extent needed; coordinating with Agencies and stakeholders as necessary; construction of seepage and stability berms and buried curb walls in various locations; researching, potholing, removing and replacing existing utilities; protecting existing utilities, reusing excavated soils that meet specification criteria for reuse as levee fill; importing soil for levee fill as necessary; managing and disposing of excess excavated soils; removing all temporary facilities; and restoring and vegetating all disturbed areas. All contractor and subcontractor personnel performing work under this contract must be citizens of the United States. U.S. citizenship is a prerequisite for obtaining the required Department of War (DoW) personnel security clearances. The contractor shall be responsible for ensuring all personnel comply with this requirement and all applicable federal security regulations. The solicitation is anticipated to proceed as a total small business set-aside and is estimated to be issued late- November 2026 with bids due tentatively in late-December 2026. The IFB will be issued on the Government Point of Entry known as SAM.gov and will establish a firm bid due date/time. The magnitude of construction for the anticipated project is between $16,000,000 and $20,000,000. This solicitation is anticipated to be issued using the North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code 237990 (Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction). The small business size standard is $45,000,000. Product Service Code is Y1LC (Construction of Tunnels and Subsurface Structures). If applicable, the site visit date, time and location will be identified in the solicitation. BE ADVISED THAT THIS PROJECT MAY BE DELAYED, CANCELLED OR REVISED AT ANY TIME DURING THE PRE-SOLICITATION, SOLICITATION, SELECTION, EVALUATION, NEGOTIATION AND/OR FINAL AWARD PROCESS. The only INTERESTED VENDORS LISTS (plan-holder's/bidder's list) are available via SAM.gov. Contractors are responsible for self-identifying as interested vendors and viewing other interested vendors. Contractors should check SAM.gov frequently for any changes to the interested vendors list and notice. PLEASE DO NOT request a copy of the solicitation, or draft plans and specifications, as they are not currently available. Any available technical data required to respond to the solicitation will be furnished as part of the solicitation. Following solicitation release, all responsible sources may submit a bid that shall be considered by the agency. This project and/or the anticipated solicitation may be changed, delayed, or canceled at any time. All prospective Offerors and their Subcontractors must be registered in SAM and the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) websites to download solicitation information. Solicitation documents, plans, and specifications will only be available to be downloaded from PIEE, which may be accessed at https://piee.eb.mil/. Registration should be completed one (1) week prior to the anticipated solicitation release date. USACE-SPK will not notify Offerors of any changes to the solicitation; Offerors must monitor PIEE and SAM for the solicitation to be posted, and for any posted changes or amendments.

title: Finland – Refuse and waste related services – Lääke- ja särmäisjäte sekä tietosuoja- ja tietoturvajätteet
description: Keski-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialueelle (jäljempänä Keusote) tulee toiminnassaan lääke- ja särmäisjätettä sekä tietosuoja- ja tietoturvajätteitä. Keusote pyytää sitovaa tarjoustanne Lääke- ja särmäisjätteiden sekä tietosuoja- ja tietoturvajätteiden noudosta ja asianmukaisen loppukäsittelyn hoitamisesta. Lääke- ja särmäisjätteen kohdeyksiköt ovat Keusoten Hyvinkään, Järvenpään, Nurmijärven ja Tuusulan kotihoidon, Ikääntyneiden- , kehitysvammaisten- ja vammaisten asumispalveluyksiköistä sekä avopalveluista. Katso kohdeliitteet Liite 1 ja Liite 2. Tietoturvajätteen kohde listaus eroaa lääke- ja särmäisjätteen kohdelistauksesta. Hankinnan tarkemmat kuvaukset Lääke- ja särmäisjäte Palvelu sisältää lääkejätteen sekä särmäis- ja viiltävän jätteen keräysastioiden toimittamisen, jätteiden noudon ja asianmukaisen loppukäsittelyn voimassa olevan lainsäädännön, sekä viranomaismääräysten mukaisesti. Palveluntuottajan tulee huolehtia koko käsittelyketjun jäljitettävyydestä ja raportoida tilaajalle jätteen määristä ja käsittelytavoista (katso tarkemmin sopimusluonnos). Tietosuoja Tietosuojajätteen noudon ja käsittelyn osalta palveluun kuuluu myös käsittelyn dokumentointi. Palvelu sisältää tietosuoja- ja tietoturvajätteen keräysastioiden toimittamisen, jätteiden noudon, kuljetuksen, käsittelyn ja asianmukaisen loppukäsittelyn voimassa olevan lainsäädännön, sekä viranomaismääräysten mukaisesti. Käsittelytodistuksesta tulee näkyä noutopäivä, käsittelypaikka ja hävitysmenetelmä. Palveluntuottajan tulee noudattaa Keusoten tietosuoja- ja tietoturvavaatimuksia, sekä voimassa olevaa tietosuojalainsäädäntöä. Palveluntuottajan henkilöstö sitoutuu käsittelemään tehtävissään mahdollisesti saamansa tiedot luottamuksellisesti. Tietoja saa käsitellä ainoastaan palvelun toteuttamisen edellyttämässä laajuudessa. Salassapito- ja tietosuojavelvoitteet jatkuvat myös sopimuskauden päättymisen jälkeen. Tarkempi kuvaus esitetty erillisissä sopimusluonnoksissa (Liite 3 ja Liite 4) Sopimukset tehdään toistaiseksi voimassaolevina. Sopimus tehdään alustavasti alkaen 1.4.2027 riippuen allekirjoitusajankohdasta. Hankinnassa on kaksi erillistä osaa: Osa 1 Lääke- ja särmäisjäte ja osa 2 Tietosuoja- ja tietoturvajätteet. Hankinnan osia 1 ja 2 voi tarjota erikseen. HUOM! Mikäli jollekin liitteelle ei ole paikkaa se liitetään tarjouspyynnön liitteeksi kohtaan välilehdellä ”lähetys”, kohtaan ”muut liitteet”.

title: DCNG Laundry Services
description: The District of Columbia National Guard (DCNG) requires wash and fold laundry service. The contractor shall deliver clean (free of any detectable chemical residue�oil, grease, petroleum products, etc.) items and pick up soiled items daily. Pickup and delivery services shall be provided at Government-directed locations throughout the National Capital Region (NCR). The current hotel locations are listed in Technical Exhibit 2 of the PWS. Laundry services will include laundering of military equipment, clothing, towels, and bed linen. The contractor will pick up, transport, clean, and deliver as agreed upon with the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR). The contractor shall return the laundry within forty-eight (48) to seventy-two (72) hours of pickup unless otherwise approved in writing by the COR. Locations will be coordinated between the Contractor and the COR per scheduled pickup. The Government will evaluate offers for award purposes by adding the total price for all options to the total price for the basic requirement. Evaluation of options will not obligate the Government to exercise the option. The government will then evaluate other factors (examples but not limited to: past performance, contractor�s resources to meet PWS deliverables, prime doing a majority of the work, location of laundry facility, work experience, process to ensure timely pick up and drop off of cleaned laundry, process to maintain accountability of laundry, process to compensate for loss) of each offerors quote to verify if a higher cost is justified to provide the best value to the government. title: J012--Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning, Kitchen Fire Suppression System Service, and Portable Fire Extinguisher Service
description: 1. Title: Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning, Kitchen Fire Suppression System Service, and Portable Fire Extinguisher Service 2. Background: Per NFPA 96, the new Food Services Center (Bldg. 211), and JLM dietetics are required to have their kitchen hoods cleaned semiannually due to limited grease use and/or limited meal service. The hoods for JLM, B170, and 202 require quarterly cleaning due to the heavy grease operations. During regular cleaning, the hood system must be inspected, tested and maintained. Per NFPA and regulatory requirements, kitchen fire suppression systems shall be inspected and serviced at a minimum of every 6 months to ensure proper operation and life safety compliance. Given that the kitchen fire suppression systems will be inspected, government is including the inspection, testing and maintenance of the portable fire extinguisher. Per NFPA and regulatory requirements, portable fire extinguishers shall be inspected, serviced, and hydrotested to ensure proper operation. 3. Purpose: The Network Contracting Office (NCO) 16, located at Galleria Financial Center, 5075 Westheimer Rd, Ste 750, Houston, TX 77030, hereby issues the following Sources Sought to Request Information (RFI) with the intent of determining the contractor interest, capabilities, qualifications of potential businesses and estimated industry pricing information for market research and estimated budgetary purpose for Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning, Kitchen Fire Suppression System Service, and Portable Fire Extinguisher Service 4. Requirement summary: The Government presently considers fire-protection equipment inspection, testing, preventive maintenance, recharge, hydrostatic testing, repair, authorized replacement, and restoration to be the predominant purpose of the integrated requirement. Accordingly, North American Industry Classification System code 811310 is proposed.� The anticipated requirement combines recurring commercial services at the John L. McClellan Memorial Veterans Hospital in Little Rock and the Eugene J. Towbin Healthcare Center in North Little Rock. The draft scope includes:� Quarterly and semiannual cleaning of identified commercial kitchen hoods, plenums, ducts, fans, dampers, and related exhaust-system components.� Semiannual inspection, testing, maintenance, tagging, and documentation for 10 wet-chemical kitchen fire suppression systems.� Inspection, maintenance, recharge, hydrostatic testing, repair, authorized replacement, pickup, return, tagging, and asset-level reporting for approximately 948 portable fire extinguishers across listed classes and locations.� Qualified personnel, manufacturer authorization when required, calibrated test equipment, safety controls, chemical and waste management, impairment coordination, incident reporting support, and digital service records.� A potential base period with four one-year option periods. The final contract structure and quantities have not been determined.� Respondents should address the ability to perform all three principal service areas as the prime contractor and identify any anticipated subcontracting or teaming arrangement. 5. Requested capability information: Interested parties should submit a concise capability statement, preferably no more than 10 pages excluding cover page and supporting certifications. Clearly identify proprietary information. Address each item below in the order listed.� Legal business name, physical address, website, and primary point of contact, including name, title, telephone number, and email address.� Unique Entity Identifier and Commercial and Government Entity code.� Business size under proposed North American Industry Classification System code 811310 and any recommended alternative code.� Socioeconomic status, including small business, veteran-owned small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business, women-owned small business, economically disadvantaged women-owned small business, Historically Underutilized Business Zone small business, 8(a) participant, or small disadvantaged business. Identify current Small Business Administration VetCert status when claiming veteran-owned or service-disabled veteran-owned status.� Whether the respondent intends to perform as the prime contractor and the approximate percentage of work the respondent expects to perform with its own employees.� Capability to provide all required service areas at both campuses, including after-hours kitchen exhaust cleaning and normal-business-hours fire protection services.� Current qualifications and certifications relevant to National Fire Protection Association Standards 10, 17A, and 96; Underwriters Laboratories 300-listed systems; Ansul and PyroChem systems; kitchen exhaust cleaning; extinguisher maintenance; and hydrostatic testing. Identify whether credentials are held by the respondent or a proposed subcontractor.� At least two recent and relevant contracts or projects completed within the past five years. Include customer, contract or project identifier if releasable, period of performance, dollar magnitude or range, scope, locations, and customer point of contact if authorized.� Available staffing, mobilization timeframe, service radius, emergency or impairment response capability, and ability to maintain recurring schedules at both campuses.� Quality-control approach, asset tracking, service-report format, deficiency management, chain-of-custody controls, and ability to provide searchable Microsoft Excel or Portable Document Format reports.� Any contract vehicle available to the Government, including Federal Supply Schedule contract information, if applicable.� 6. Licenses, certifications, and technical qualifications: Respondents shall identify the licenses, certifications, manufacturer authorizations, and technical qualifications currently available to perform the draft requirement. A credential matrix is acceptable at the Sources Sought stage. Do not submit Social Security numbers, dates of birth, home addresses, or other unnecessary personal information. Current Arkansas Fire Protection Licensing Board company Certificate of Registration for portable fire-extinguisher systems and fixed fire-suppression systems. Current individual Arkansas licenses for proposed or available technicians covering portable fire extinguishers, fixed wet-chemical fire-suppression systems, and hydrostatic testing, as applicable to assigned work. Current Ansul and Pyro-Chem manufacturer-authorized distributor, service-provider, or technician documentation applicable to the installed system models. Identify any other manufacturer authorization available. International Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning Association Certified Exhaust Cleaning Specialist, Certified Exhaust Cleaning Technician, or an equivalent nationally recognized commercial kitchen exhaust-cleaning credential for the proposed crew leader or onsite supervisor. A Professional Exhaust Cleaning Technician designation should be identified as a designation rather than represented as a full certification. Current Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration Requalifier Identification Number approval for any facility that will inspect, test, mark, or requalify regulated cylinders. If this work will be subcontracted, identify the proposed testing facility and provide its approval information. Current Arkansas hydrostatic-testing license or certificate applicable to the cylinder classes and testing methods proposed. Current calibration certificates for pressure gauges, scales, hydrostatic-test equipment, electrical test instruments, and other measurement equipment whose accuracy affects inspection or acceptance. Relevant safety-training records, including lockout/tagout, hazard communication, personal protective equipment, fall protection or rooftop work, ladder or lift operation, respiratory protection when applicable, and spill response. Current certificate of general liability insurance and identification of workers compensation and automobile

title: H144--Steam Quality Testing Service
description: Answers and Questions in response to solicitation 36C24627Q0084 Question 1) The price schedule lists 4 JB for CLIN 0001 and for each option year CLIN (1001 4001), while the CLIN descriptions and PWS describe an annual steam quality test and audit. How many testing events per year should be priced: one annual event, or four (quarterly)? Answer 1) The solicitation has since been updated. There was an error in the first posting. To clarify the testing needs to be done quarterly over a 12 month period (4 Quarterly testings). Question 2) If the quantity is 4 JB per year, does each JB represent a full test event (dryness, non-condensable gases and the steam, condensate and water audit), or a test at one location or sterilizer? Answer 2) Each JB represent a full test event for all Locations required.� (3 each) Sterilizers and Associated Steam Traps. They also check the Condensate leaving the Sterilizers (Water Audit). Question 3) How many steam sample points are to be installed in the base year, and how many sterilizers or test points in Building 110A (CG48A) are to be tested at each event? Answer 3) There are three (3) Steam Sample Points, one on each Sterilizer. There is no need to install sample points during base year. The testing can be accomplished by removing a section of the steam piping to the Sterilizer, install testing equipment and complete testing. Upon completion, remove testing equipment and return system to per-existing alignment of system.� However, if contract wants to for ease of access they can install points at their own expense. This is not a requirement of this Solicitation. Question 4) Please confirm whether we should price the broader audit scope for four jobs per year as listed in the price schedule, or the narrower testing scope once annually as stated in the Performance Work Statement. Answer 4) 4 jobs per year

title: Sources Sought for FY26 Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway Maintenance Dredging ????????? Select Sites
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ONLY. The Savannah District Corps of Engineers is requesting information regarding the market capabilities of potential contractors that can perform maintenance and unclassified dredging on the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway (AIWW) sections of waterway Hell Gate and Florida Passage in Chatham County Georgia and Fields Cut in Jasper County South Carolina. This request does not obligate the Government in any way to post a Request for Proposal or award a contract. Information received will be considered for the purpose of market research and determining how to best move forward with the procurement. Applicable NAICS code is 237990 with a size standard of $45.0M. The potential magnitude for this requirement is estimated to be between $5,000,000 and $10,000,000. The FY26 Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway (AIWW) maintenance dredging contract provides construction services, including furnishing personnel, transportation, mobilization and demobilization, equipment and materials required in connection with maintenance dredging and incidental related work. This contract is traditionally performed with a hydraulic cutterhead dredge, but other methods will be considered. The duration is expected to be five months (165 days) from Notice to Proceed. The Savannah Districts area of responsibility (AOR) of the federally maintained channel in the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway begins in Port Royal Sound, South Carolina and ends in Cumberland Sound, Georgia. The shallow draft federally maintained channel is twelve (12) feet deep MLLW with widths from ninety (90) feet in land cuts and one hundred fifty (150) feet in natural waterways. Savannah Districts FY26 AIWW maintenance dredging work is located within the state of Georgia (Chatham County) and in the state of South Carolina (Jasper County). The Hell Gate section of waterway is to be dredged to authorized width of 150 feet and depth of 12 feet. The work also includes options to dredge the Florida Passage and the Fields Cut sections of the waterway to authorized width of 150 feet and depth of 12 feet. Approximately two hundred thousand (200,000) cubic yards of maintenance material is anticipated to be removed from the Hell Gate section of the federally maintained channel in the waterway. Approximately fifteen thousand (15,000) cubic yards of maintenance material is anticipated to be removed from the Florida Passage section of the federally maintained channel in the waterway. Approximately fifty thousand (50,000) cubic yards of maintenance material is anticipated to be removed from the Fields Cut section of the federally maintained channel in the waterway. Sediment dredged from Hell Gate may be pumped approximately four (4) miles to a Beneficial Use placement site in tidal flats east of Ogeechee Bar. Sediment dredged from Florida Passage may be pumped approximately nine (9) miles to the Beneficial Use placement site in the tidal flats east of Ogeechee Bar. Sediment dredged from Fields Cut will be pumped to the adjacent confined upland containment area DMCA 14B. The attached Request for Information should be filled out and loaded via PIEE before the sources sought close on 20 November 2026, 11:00 a.m. (EST). title: Rate Intervention and Utility Market Analysis
description: STATEMENT OF WORK for NAVFACSYSCOM Utility Rate Intervention and Utility Market Analysis I. Utility Rate Intervention (C.1 through C.9) C.1 DEFINITIONS The following acronyms or words shall have the corresponding meanings: NAVFACSYSCOM: Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Headquarters FEA: Federal Executive Agencies COTR: Contracting Officer�s Technical Representative SOW: Statement of Work T.O.: Task Order - A task order is a document (DD Form 1155) prepared by the Contracting Officer that is issued to the contractor and unilaterally orders work to be performed. C.2 INTRODUCTION a. The Department of the Navy, Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFACSYSCOM) purchases utility services (electricity, water and natural gas) more than $1 billion annually. NAVFACSYSCOM intervenes in the utility regulatory ratemaking process before various federal, state or local authorities. A major part of NAVFACSYSCOM mission is to protect the Navy�s interests in utility cases, to supply technical support for Navy representation before regulatory bodies, and to participate in regulatory proceedings to ensure that the utility rates are reasonably close to the utility�s cost of providing the service, that they are not unduly discriminatory, and that the rates are just and reasonable. Frequently, NAVFACSYSCOM encounters situations where its participation in the regulatory proceedings concerning utility rate applications is impeded because of manpower, time or specific technical limitations. On occasion, NAVFACSYSCOM contracts professional expertise in certain disciplines in support of its own capabilities. The area in which expert assistance may be required is Cost Allocation and Rate Design. b. Offerors must explicitly state how they can provide the required analysis, testimony, exhibits schedules and work papers or studies within a period not more than thirty calendar days from the date of receiving the assignment and pertinent original case data. Offerors should present in detail their technical and managerial plans for accomplishing such tasks in a timely manner. C.3 SCOPE OF WORK The following tasks are representative of work the contractor may be required to perform. Each task order (T.O.) will include a Statement of Work (SOW) which specifically identifies the requirements of each case. a. Review and analyze the utility�s application including its filing, testimony, exhibits, and other rate case data, work papers, studies, and submit discovery questions, if necessary, as they relate to Cost Allocation and Rate Design. b. Prepare suggested cross-examination questions for all witnesses of adversary parties. c. Prepare testimony and attend hearings if the regulatory authority requires oral presentation of the testimony. If such is required, the Contractor�s witness shall also provide case counsel with technical support. The witness will also be subject to cross-examination by any party to the proceedings. Testimony is to be presented on behalf of the Navy, DOD, and all other FEA�s for consideration by the regulatory authority. d. Provide technical notes for the preparation of legal briefs. e. Analyze orders of the regulatory body and prepare a final report identifying the treatment of the issue presented by the Navy and its resultant cost reduction. C.4 GOVERNMENT FURNISHED PROPERTY None C.5 CONTRACTOR FURNISHED ITEMS The contractor shall provide all equipment, materials, and services to perform the requirements of this contract. C.6 STUDIES AND ANALYSIS REPORTS a. Certain utility issues may require a preliminary analysis report to be performed for a determination to be made as to whether there is a need for intervention or other Navy action. b. The Contractor may, on his own, identify potential issues that can be challenged in testimony, an estimate of the cost savings if the challenged issues are successfully litigated and a commentary regarding the likelihood of success in the challenge of each issue and bring them to the attention of the NAVFACSYSCOM without being solicited. c. The Contractor shall perform utility-related studies as may be required by the government. The deliverable item shall be a report. C.7 ANALYSIS, DISCOVERY, TESTIMONY, CROSS-EXAMINATION, HEARINGS, BRIEFS AND ORDER EVALUATIONS a. DISCOVERY (1) The Contractor shall provide in writing, one copy each, to the COTR and the case counsel, simultaneously. All requests for data, documents and information to be served on the utility or other parties shall be provided within the time constraints established in the procedural order and paragraph C.8. (2) The Contractor shall avoid �canned� data requests as much as possible and shall restrict the requests to those that would assist in the preparation of the Navy�s case. (3) The Contractor shall integrate responses to discovery requests in developing Navy�s testimony and brief preparation. (4) The Contractor shall prepare proper responses to discovery requests served on the Navy. Two copies of the responses shall be provided to the COTR unless otherwise directed. b. TESTIMONY. The Contractor shall prepare and deliver testimony, exhibits and schedules, and, if required, surrebuttal testimony on issues within the scope of the contract. A draft of the prepared testimony shall be presented by the Contractor to the COTR for review, discussion, and modification where needed. The Contractor may be directed to submit a second draft, if necessary. When the COTR is satisfied with the testimony, the Contractor shall be instructed to proceed with the final version. No changes of any nature shall be made to the testimony after the COTR approval without his express authorization. Draft and final testimony shall be submitted in strict adherence to the dates as will be communicated to the Contractor. Final testimony shall be prepared in the format and in the number of copies as required by the regulatory authority and will be communicated to the Contractor. Information will be communicated by the NAVFACSYSCOM analysts via e-mail or telephone within the time constraints established in the procedural order and paragraph C.8. c. CROSS EXAMINATION. The Contractor shall prepare proposed cross-examination questions with anticipated answers based on the testimony, exhibits and schedules filed by witnesses to be examined. The prepared cross-examination questions shall identify the ultimate point to be developed because of a successful cross-examination, the detailed reasons for asking them, expected responses, and alternative and follow-up questions. Questions are not to be restricted only to those issues addressed in Navy�s case. A copy of the proposed cross examination questions shall be submitted to the COTR and case counsel simultaneously. The Contractor shall be informed of the dates and places of examination of witnesses. The Contractor�s attendance at the cross-examination hearings may or may not be required depending on the particulars of each rate case as will be communicated to the Contractor by NAVFACSYSCOM analysts via e-mail or telephonically within the time constraints established in the procedural order and paragraph C.8. d. HEARINGS. The Contractor�s expert witnesses shall appear before the regulatory body to support their testimony. For this phase, the Contractor shall prepare a summary of the testimony to be delivered at the hearings. The summary shall be reduced to writing and forwarded to the COTR at least five working days prior to the delivery of the testimony on the witness stand. The summary may be waived if such is not the practice of the regulatory authority. The witnesses shall be available to present the testimony and undergo the examination by other parties or to attend Navy�s cross-examination of its adversaries at the times and places set by the cognizant regulatory body. e. title: Canadian Defence Academy Research Paper: Understanding Resilience in the Canadian Armed Forces: A Multi-Level Framework
description: This Statement of Work (SOW) defines the scope, deliverables, and requirements for research examining resilience across multiple levels of analysis to inform understandings of resilience as a component of military effectiveness, readiness, adaptation, and preparedness to inform updated methods and approaches supporting CAF professional development. The National Security Institute seeks an academic analysis of resilience concepts and frameworks to support professional military education (PME), professional development (PD), and leader development activities by improving understanding of the relationship between individual, organizational, institutional, and societal resilience.

title: Canadian Defence Academy Research Paper - National Resilience and Whole-of-Society Defence: Nordic Approaches and Implications for the CAF
description: This Statement of Work (SOW) defines the scope, deliverables, and requirements for researching national resilience and whole-of-society approaches to security and defence among selected Nordic allies to inform Professional Military Education (PME) and Professional Development (PD). The National Security Institute seeks an academic assessment of national resilience concepts, structures, and practices to improve understanding of how military organizations contribute to broader societal resilience and preparedness.

title: Canadian Defence Academy Research Paper: Cognitive Resilience and Cognitive Superiority in the CAF Context
description: This Statement of Work (SOW) defines the scope, deliverables, and requirements for examining cognitive resilience and cognitive superiority as components of military effectiveness, decision-making, adaptation, and leader development to inform Professional Military Education (PME) and Professional Development (PD). The National Security Institute seeks an academic assessment of cognitive resilience and cognitive superiority concepts to support PME, PD, and leader development initiatives across the Defence Team.

title: Canadian Defence Academy Research Paper - Hybrid Threats, National Resilience, and Whole-of-Society Understanding
description: This Statement of Work (SOW) defines the scope, deliverables, and requirements for examining how governments, military organizations, and societies understand and assess hybrid threats through a whole-of-society lens to inform Professional Military Education (PME) and Professional Development (PD). The National Security Institute seeks an academic analysis of hybrid threats and whole-of-society approaches to support PME, PD, and leader development activities focused on resilience, preparedness, and strategic understanding.

title: Canadian Defence Academy Research Paper - Cognitive Warfare, Disinformation, and Defence Team Resilience
description: This Statement of Work (SOW) defines the scope, deliverables, and requirements for examining cognitive warfare, disinformation, and influence activities affecting military personnel, defence institutions, and broader society to inform Professional Military Education (PME) and Professional Development (PD). The National Security Institute seeks an analysis of cognitive warfare and information-based threats to support PME, PD, and leader development activities focused on strengthening Defence Team resilience.
